theorem effectiveEpi_tfae
    {B X : Profinite.{u}} (π : X ⟶ B) :
    TFAE
    [ EffectiveEpi π
    , Epi π
    , Function.Surjective π
    ] := by
  tfae_have 1 → 2 := fun _ ↦ inferInstance

  tfae_finish
findings.problem: The statement is specialised to `Profinite`, but the proof uses no Profinite-specific structure except `Profinite.epi_iff_surjective`. The `1 → 2` step is the generic instance `EffectiveEpi → Epi`, the `3 → 1` step is the generic `CompHausLike.effectiveEpiStruct`, and the `2 ↔ 3` step is just the surjectivity characterization of epis. The very same proof appears verbatim in `CompHaus.effectiveEpi_tfae` (CompHaus/EffectiveEpi.lean:39-49) and `Stonean.effectiveEpi_tfae` (Stonean/EffectiveEpi.lean:34-44), and the derived `PreservesEffectiveEpis`/`ReflectsEffectiveEpis` instances at lines 47-53 are also instances of the same pattern. The only genuinely category-specific input is the hypothesis `Epi f → Function.Surjective f`, which is already the parameter shape used by the generic `CompHausLike.preregular`.
findings.proposed_change:
State the result once at the `CompHausLike` level and keep the Profinite version as a one-line corollary:

```lean
namespace CompHausLike
variable {P : TopCat.{u} → Prop}
theorem effectiveEpi_tfae
    (hs : ∀ ⦃X Y : CompHausLike.{u} P⦄ (f : X ⟶ Y), Epi f → Function.Surjective f)
    {B X : CompHausLike.{u} P} (π : X ⟶ B) :
    TFAE [EffectiveEpi π, Epi π, Function.Surjective π] := by
  tfae_have 1 → 2 := fun _ ↦ inferInstance
  tfae_have 2 ↔ 3 := ⟨hs π, epi_of_surjective π⟩
  tfae_have 3 → 1 := fun hπ ↦ ⟨⟨effectiveEpiStruct π hπ⟩⟩
  tfae_finish
```

using `CompHausLike.epi_of_surjective` (CompHausLike/Basic.lean:209) for the reverse direction and `CompHausLike.effectiveEpiStruct` (CompHausLike/EffectiveEpi.lean:36) for `3 → 1`. The specialization in this file becomes `CompHausLike.effectiveEpi_tfae (fun f hf ↦ (epi_iff_surjective f).mp hf) π` (and analogously for `CompHaus`, `Stonean` via their `epi_iff_surjective`). The two `PreservesEffectiveEpis`/`ReflectsEffectiveEpis` instances can then be phrased generically with the same hypothesis, since they only pass through `Surjective`.
findings.benefit: One theorem and one proof instead of three near-identical copies, immediately usable for any `CompHausLike P` category (including `LightProfinite`) that supplies the surjectivity direction on epis. It also makes explicit to readers that nothing about total disconnectedness is used, and keeps the Profinite-specific API (`Profinite.effectiveEpi_tfae`, still used in Condensed/Equivalence.lean and Condensed/Discrete/Colimit.lean) as a thin wrapper.
